item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Creepy dead kids locked up in a box. Not a fan.

First:
SCP-747-B9 is mentioned as a procedure but is never elaborated on. Instead it is replaced with the following paragraph. So why refer to this non-existent material at all?

SCP-747-B9 would be assumed to contain special measures for dealing with personnel targeted by the SCP and therefore contain information not present in this skip. As this stands -B9 is worthless as the Procedures directly reveals the most basic content -B9 would withhold from lower level researchers.

Second:
Why does this skip have it's own Task force? Why doesn't this Task Force follow the naming and operating conventions of other Task Forces in-universe?
Does SCP-747 so frequently breach containment that the Foundation keeps five to eight personnel on alert?

Third:
"The commonality of the children, according to research, is that they all owned a doll precious to them at their time of death." Huh? This line relates toward back to the theme of Dolls in the article. But is never itself highlighted by the rest of the article in turn. What is it about the Children's attachment to dolls that drives them to maintain this hive-mind predation of Adults?

"Each instance of SCP-747 cannot speak," How does the Foundation know this if the Children only recognize and interact with Adults when they are performing their Juju?

"most people describe a feeling of 'thoughtlessness' or 'blankness' when in contact with SCP-747" Does this condition affect any adults whenever there is proximity contact with 747? Or is the condition limited to the event of 747's Juju? Either way, wouldn't this be forewarned in the Containment Procedures(and or in the -B9 material?)

Fourth:
I agree that Document 747-B4 should be fleshed out. It is implied the Foundation has some evidence suggesting the Juju'ed dolls are conscious. I would like to see that elaborated on.

Five:
The second picture is out of place physically with the rest of the document. Perhaps setting on the left side of with the section elaborating the transformation process?

Altogether. A suitable mysterious phenomenon that lacks real teeth and consistent internal structure. A good idea that needs better formatting and an elaborated story.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Not necessarily. Not only verisimilitude.

There are a lot of us who would love to have those documents to pour over, to really dig our teeth into things and understand more of what's going on. Those types of documents can be interesting, and well received, when they're well written and thought out. They don't necessarily allow you to fully understand the SCP in question, in and of itself, but they give context, and lead you further down the rabbit hole.

Good articles aren't generally the lesser for their absence, though. Here, we're told that there has been due consideration given to a matter which warrants it, and those findings are available for consideration, only elsewhere. Sad days for us, who can't find it, and are left to wonder.

So it does add to verisimilitude, but it isn't absent because it would be boring to read. Consider the context, here.

Subject transforms fully into a doll within twenty-four (24) hours. At this point SCP-747 will treat them as any other doll. It is currently theorized that the subject is no longer conscious or 'alive' in any sense. See Document 747-B4.

That would seem to imply that the Foundation has some pretty significant evidence suggesting the dolls are still conscious, on some level. How would they know that? EEG readings seem to persist only until the transformation is complete, at which point they may reasonably be inferred to halt, and that makes sense. There's only stuffing and straw for insides, now, no longer any brain, and therefore no electrical impulses for an EEG to pick up. Yet, Document 747-B4 would appear to contain evidence there is still something like a mind in there. So, how much do we know, about the nature of this remnant? Its eyes are buttons, and those don't see, but then, straw and rags don't generally think, either. So do they still see, or sense anything else at all? If not, what's the nature of that oblivion, to them? Empty purgatory, saccharine bliss, agony, whatever 747 wants it to be, whatever SCP-747 thinks that it is… all are possibilities.

So no, out-of-universe, the document, at least in this instance, isn't withheld because we wouldn't be interested. Exactly the opposite.

item.content:encoded: I've added a few sentences to tie it in. I like the challenge and don't think there is really a line between creepypasta and SCP. The challenge is to creep and frighten without ever using subjective terms, and it's plainly fun. I plan to add a few documents to perhaps help the 'creepasta vs scp' conflict, but I simply don't see it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: As I said in chat, the ideas are good. But the problems I mentioned also remain. As people have commented, this is kind of arbitrary, and you've said you've been having a hard time working in something to tie it together. These problems stem from the fact that the SCP, in its current form, is a poor match for the clinical style of an SCP article. It's doing pretty well, but people are upvoting it on the strength of the ideas and the basically decent writing. I still feel it would work better as a creepypasta, where you wouldn't be constrained by the format and tone of an SCP, which I feel clashes with what you're trying to evoke.
